story.narrative:
Mateo Villareal died on 1 February 2026 in Manila, Philippines, leaving a will executed on 1 June 2025. Mateo was the legitimate child of Ramon and Clara Villareal. Ramon was himself born outside marriage to Tomas and Rosa Villareal, with both filiations proved; Clara was the legitimate child of Luz Santiago. Ramon died in 2023 and Rosa in 2024. Mateo died unmarried and without descendants, survived by Clara, paternal grandfather Tomas and maternal grandmother Luz. Tomas claims a parental share by representing Ramon. All assets were self-acquired; probate, capacity and acceptance are stipulated, and the accounting date is 30 June 2026. Gross assets are PHP 20,000,000 and total liabilities are PHP 2,000,000, with no additional debts or donations to collate.

The will confirms Clara's unburdened legitime and leaves PHP 6,000,000 to Rosa, with Tomas substituting on predecease, repudiation or incapacity. This gift, including the substitute's gift, depends on the city's independent digitization center opening by 30 June 2026; it opened on 15 March and Tomas accepted. A separate PHP 3,000,000 legacy to Luz must be returned with fruits and interest if she deliberately destroys the identified family archive within two years. Luz accepted and furnished security; no destruction has occurred. Compute the distribution of Mateo Villareal's estate.

story.narrative:
Lucia Navarro died on 1 February 2026 in Manila, Philippines, leaving a will executed on 1 June 2025. Lucia was the legitimate child of Pedro Navarro and Elisa Cruz, both of whom predeceased her. She died unmarried and without descendants. Paternal grandmother Rosa Navarro also predeceased her. Paternal grandfather Tomas Navarro and maternal grandparents Jaime and Teresa Cruz survived; all three are in the same ascending degree. Her assets were self-acquired, filiation and probate are stipulated, and the accounting date is 30 June 2026. Gross assets are PHP 26,000,000 and total liabilities are PHP 2,000,000, with no additional debts or donations to collate.

The will confirms the grandparents' unburdened legitimes and makes separate voluntary cash legacies of PHP 6,000,000 to Tomas, PHP 3,000,000 to Jaime and PHP 3,000,000 to Teresa. Each reciprocally substitutes for a beneficiary who predeceases, repudiates or cannot accept, in proportion to the accepting substitutes' original voluntary shares. Each voluntary recipient, including any substitute, must submit an archive plan and obtain independent archivist approval. Tomas and Jaime complied and accepted. Teresa formally repudiated only her separate voluntary legacy after Lucia's death; all three accepted their unburdened legitimes. Compute the distribution of Lucia Navarro's estate.

Under Articles 889 and 890, the PHP 12,000,000 reserve is first divided equally between paternal and maternal lines. Tomas receives the paternal PHP 6,000,000; Jaime and Teresa divide the maternal PHP 6,000,000 equally. This division by lines is not representation or per stirpes under Articles 972–974. Article 987 supplies the parallel intestate rule, not a second allocation to add.

story.narrative:

story.narrative:
Teresa Garcia died on 1 February 2026 in Manila, Philippines, leaving a will executed on 1 June 2025. Teresa was jointly and validly adopted by Victor and Lina Garcia under Republic Act No. 11642 in 2023. The adoption was final, never rescinded and not a stepparent adoption. Teresa died unmarried and without descendants. Both adopters and Victor's mother, Sofia Garcia, survived, as did Teresa's biological father Jose Cruz; biological mother Bea Reyes died in 2025. All estate assets were self-acquired; probate, capacity and acceptance are stipulated. The accounting date is 30 June 2026. Gross assets are PHP 22,000,000 and total liabilities are PHP 2,000,000, with no additional debts or donations to collate.

The will confirms Victor's and Lina's unburdened legitimes and leaves a PHP 10,000,000 cash legacy to Bea. Jose is expressly substituted for Bea upon predecease, repudiation or incapacity. The recipient must submit a preservation plan and obtain independent museum-board approval by 30 June 2026; this requirement expressly binds Jose. He submitted the plan, obtained approval on 1 April 2026 and accepted. Assess the respective positions of the adopters, the adoptive grandmother and the biological parents in carrying out the will. Compute the distribution of Teresa Garcia's estate.
